data.summary: E083 experiment: view-count principle on aviation maintenance fault codes. Key results: G1 PASS (30≥30 both arms), G2 FAIL (0.70 accuracy vs 0.85 threshold), G3 REPORTING: treatment 63.3% served (19/30), 10% partially_served (3/30), 26.7% unserved (8/30); control 50.0% served (15/30), 36.7% partially_served (11/30), 13.3% unserved (4/30). Key differentiator: 10% partially_served rate for aviation maintenance vs 0% for lab instruments and 36.7% for general computer errors — shows the view-count principle has a consistent binary→partial→spectrum pattern across technical domains (increasing partial rate as domains become less code-structured). G4 FAIL (14/20 top-arrival vs threshold 17/20). Decision: hold - principle generalizes to aviation domain with intermediate partial-served rate; three-domain mapping (lab=0%, aviation=10%, general=36.7% partially_served) establishes generalization boundaries. Next fresh observation needed in new domain per D083.
